description: Path-based health policy. Journey status is derived from component status using these dependency semantics (NOT a naive 'one dep down = app down'). Architecture (components/edges/journeys) stays source-of-truth in docs/architecture/*.json; this file only encodes fallback/degrade rules and thresholds.

environment.note: Production default build = Firestore (USE_RAILWAY_API unset). Railway REST is opt-in; its journeys are only critical in REST-mode builds.

overall.rule: worst status among criticalJourneys; CRITICAL if any critical journey DOWN, DEGRADED if any DEGRADED, HEALTHY if all HEALTHY, else UNKNOWN

releaseCriticalNote: Journeys that MUST be verified to ship. UNKNOWN (not verified) BLOCKS release (Phase 13) — distinct from DOWN. j-ai-summary is NOT release-critical (heuristic fallback). j-legacy-cutover is a migration gate, not per-build critical.

platform.note: Components scoped to one platform block only that platform (e.g. Apple App Store fail -> iOS BLOCK, Android may be READY). Everything else (Firebase core, Firestore, hosting) blocks BOTH. Firebase Auth carries both Google+Apple, so it blocks both (can't distinguish provider live).

j-owner-start.softDegradeNote: appConfig read is fail-open; Firestore down degrades gate check but app still opens

fallbackGroups.note: f.html REST fallback via meta tag; if Firestore down but Railway up -> DEGRADED (fallback available)

j-public-feedback-rest.note: Only live in REST-mode builds / when f.html has ftm-public-api meta

j-purchase-credit.note: Server-side IAP verification (iapVerify) is now wired + code-verified (ci-functions-iap + flutter iap tests). Live status stays UNKNOWN/NOT VERIFIED until a real sandbox E2E runs (syn-iap-verify, not-configured) — security-architecture-fixed != store-purchase-E2E-verified.

j-ai-summary.softDegradeNote: AI proxy/OpenAI down -> DEGRADED (heuristic fallback keeps the journey working)

staticRisks.title: IAP purchase not bound to the buyer identity (no appAccountToken / obfuscatedAccountId check)
staticRisks.evidence: functions/src/index.ts (iapVerify grants to request.auth.uid; receipt/token ownership not verified)
staticRisks.resolution: Bind the purchase to the buyer: verify Apple appAccountToken (StoreKit2) / Google obfuscatedExternalAccountId == uid. Client already sets PurchaseParam.applicationUserName=uid; surface + check it server-side. Legacy Apple verifyReceipt cannot expose this, so Apple binding needs StoreKit2.
staticRisks.note: NOT a free-credit hole: processedPurchases is global (one store txId = one credit system-wide), so this is first-claim-wins, not multiplication. Risk is receipt theft / credit misattribution (needs another user's receipt). P0 (verification+idempotency) stays closed. Decide before broad launch.

staticRisks.title: Apple receipt bundle_id not explicitly checked in verifyApple
staticRisks.note: Mitigated: APPLE_SHARED_SECRET is app-specific, so a receipt from another app fails verifyReceipt (21004). Defense-in-depth: also assert receipt.bundle_id == expected bundle. Non-blocking.

staticRisks.title: Railway auth is a dev-login bridge only (real OAuth is a TODO)
Store build history unknown — cannot confirm next iOS CFBundleVersion / Android versionCode is monotonic
staticRisks.resolution: Confirm the last published build numbers in App Store Connect / Play Console; ensure the new build increments both, and pubspec +BUILD == kAppBuild.
staticRisks.note: Release gate cannot pick a next build number. User action.

staticRisks.title: Production read-only audit of users where isPremium==true not yet run
staticRisks.resolution: Run the read-only audit (Firebase Console query users where isPremium==true, or admin script); migrate any found (grant credits) before the credit-only rules go live.
staticRisks.note: Needs production read credentials — not run by ops (no prod creds). User action.

liveDriftBlockers.title: appConfig/version public-read allowed in repo but DENIED live (403) — deployment drift
liveDriftBlockers.triggersWhen: node-firestore-rules live check returns 403 RULES_DENY (deployed rules deny the appConfig public read)
liveDriftBlockers.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-16: deployed firestore:rules to feedbacktome-79655 via the authorized Firebase deploy account; live appConfig/version now returns 404 (read allowed), not 403. This blocker only re-fires if the live check again reports RULES_DENY.
liveDriftBlockers.note: Rule ACCESS health. Distinct from version-config-document-missing (CONFIG health). VersionGate is fail-open, so even a rules-deny does NOT lock users — it silently disables the gate. Sourced from the live check, not static.

liveDriftBlockers.title: appConfig/version document does not exist in production — min-version gate INACTIVE
liveDriftBlockers.triggersWhen: appConfig live read returns 404 (APPCONFIG_MISSING): rules ALLOW the read but the config doc is not created yet
liveDriftBlockers.resolution: After the Bridge Release build is confirmed (see build-number-unconfirmed), create appConfig/version { minSupportedBuild <= BridgeBuild, latestBuild } via Admin SDK / Firebase console. Do NOT create it before the build number is known (a too-high minSupportedBuild would lock current clients).
liveDriftBlockers.note: CONFIGURATION health, NOT rule health. Rules drift is RESOLVED (read allowed → 404). VersionGate is FAIL-OPEN, so the owner app still opens; the min-version gate is merely INACTIVE until the doc exists. Coupled to build-number-unconfirmed. Sourced from the live check (errorCode APPCONFIG_MISSING).

releaseGate.note: A release-critical journey that is UNKNOWN (not verified — e.g. synthetic auth/IAP not configured) BLOCKS release (P1), distinct from DOWN. CI evidence must be PASS and match the release commit SHA (stale => blocker).
